claims.statement: For uniform x in [0, r) and Q = [x]P on the fixed NIST P-256 generator P, the single-seed Floyd adding walk specified in proof.md returns the scalar with probability at least 0.39 over the uniform production challenge and fresh algorithm coins. Total classical work is at most W = 72912983316395138025578212591182278225982 target-group-operation equivalents, including every online step, the jump setup, verification, and the instruction reserve. The declared score 135743300/1000000 = 135.743300 is a ceiling of log2(W) at resolution 10^(-6). Peak memory is at most 2^20 bytes. Preprocessing independent of the challenge is at most W_pre = 1073742 target-group-operation equivalents (log2 ceiling 20.034216) and is included in W. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The figure 0.39 is a lower bound under the random-mapping comparison stated in proof.md; it is not a theorem that the adding walk is a random mapping, and no production discrete logarithm is computed.

experiments.purpose: Recompute W from the public order and the instruction constants, check that the declared rational is a 10^(-6) ceiling of log2(W), and recover scalars on three prime-order additive groups. This does not establish production mixing, memory, or cost.
